quest.title: The Last Turnfire Night
quest.description: Having finished your preparations, the last Turnfire Night approaches...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Primogem x60, Mora x38100, Guide to Kindling x5, The Cornerstone of Stars and Flames x1, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, let's head off.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Off we go!

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Are you ready?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I still need time to prepare.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Of course, there's no rush. I can wait for you right here.

talks.objective: Head to the Turnfire Night venue
Head to the Turnfire Night venue

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Here we are.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Our honored guests have arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: I have heard much about your fine work over the past few days. I hope you'll allow us to thank you properly after tonight's ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it. Getting this huge venue ready must've been a huge task. No need to make extra work for yourselves on our account.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: If it means getting the Mountain King issue resolved, no cost is too great to bear.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: A resolution will come in due course. But every great fire starts as a tiny spark. We must take it one step at a time.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: No one would disagree with you if that were possible, Chief... But it's been far too long since we've seen a real step forward.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Look around you. Can't you see how our numbers have dwindled since the last Turnfire Night?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: The ceremony was arranged on short notice. Many are away from home, and could not make it back in time.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: That may be so, but still...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: #Good evening, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kinich! Not a moment too soon...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: #Chief Wayna, Elder Trinidad, could you give us a minute? I'd like to give {NICKNAME} a few pointers as the previous flame bearer.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Very well, but make it quick. Let me know when you're done, and we will begin the ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Let's step to the side. Has anyone gone over the key steps of the ceremony with you yet?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Elder Trinidad did. But uh... Paimon seems to have forgotten them...

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: What a surprise, the flying ant has an ant-sized brain.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: If you don't want your tongue to be burned off by the sacred flame tonight, I suggest you stay quiet.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Tch...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: See those Sacred Flame Pillars? Once you've lit the fire, go light each one up in turn.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Once that's done, head down into the cave where the Mountain King slumbers, light the braziers along the way, then bring the flame to the final altar. Then, the ceremony is complete.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds simple enough.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The process isn't complicated, but remember — you mustn't turn back at any point. If you miss a pillar, you can't light the next one then come back to it.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: You have to keep moving forward, or it's seen as disrespecting our ancestors. If that happens, you won't receive the blessing of the Turnfire, and you'll have to start over.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I made you a diagram that summarizes the steps. Take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Got it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's our part. What about you?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'll be with you the whole way, and once you've lit the altar, I'll start summoning the Rift.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: You can leave that side of things to me. Just focus on your part.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay. We'll try to remember all that and get it right first time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well then, shall we begin?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Ready when you are.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: But I think I saw Huni and the others just now, maybe you should say hi before you start. Might make you less nervous.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Just tell the chief when you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, we're ready to go.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: I'm counting on you. Don't forget what we talked about.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: By past fuel, and present flame, life marches ever on...

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: My brothers and sisters, the time has come to light the fire once again, and let the Turnfire Night shine bright in Huitztlan!

talks.objective: Light the Pillars of the Sacred Flame

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Ah, at long last, you're back.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: I hear that you've done much for our people these last few days. Everyone has nothing but praise for you.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Many young people have heard the rumors, too. They're all eager to meet our new flame bearer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, they won't have to wait long! It's almost time for the ceremony!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We really hope we can resolve the Mountain King situation quickly and smoothly. Seems like a lot of people have been worrying about it, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Haha, well, it's nearly time. So, if you're ready, then follow me to the ceremony site.

talks.objective: Go to the cave where the Mountain King slumbers

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: How are you doing? Is all in order?

talks.objective: Cleanse the Abyssal power all around and light the brazier

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: What happened to getting some rest?

choices.text: I'm still a little anxious about Enjou.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: You're cautious, like me. I get it. But don't worry — like I said, I investigated, and I'm confident he has nothing to do with the Mountain King situation.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Before he got tangled up with us, he was looking into the Mare Jivari. That's another major part of Natlan's history.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Our ancestor, Burkina once fought a campaign there alongside the five other heroes. But it's not such an easy place to get to these days.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: That's about all I know, though. I have yet to take a job that involves the Mare Jivari.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Heh, Ajaw's piqued your interest, huh? It's true that he's a relic from an earlier Saurian age, but since we're bound to each other by a contract, you can see him as my companion for now.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I know he can be awful, but don't worry. As long as I'm still around, he can't do that much damage.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...As long as you're around?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Mhm, that's a key part of the contract. Ajaw has to obey my orders and lend me his power for as long as I live.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: And after I die, Ajaw gets control of my body. That's the price.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Crazy, isn't it? That was probably the first time I really appreciated what it meant to pay a "price." Then, once I signed the contract, I received the ancient name "Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo."

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: But that's a whole other story. We can get into it another time, if you're interested.

talks.objective: Light up the last torches and altar

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr. Traveler, you look so cool today!}{F#Miss Traveler, you look so pretty today!}

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: You're gonna make sure the Mountain King never threatens us again, right?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: I believe in you! I'll be cheering you on the whole time!

talks.objective: Implement the final step of the plan

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woohoo! We've lit up the final altar!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's the Mountain King up ahead, right?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: That's him. Kongamato, king of the Yumkasaurs from five hundred years ago. He's very powerful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can tell, he's huge... Let's tread carefully. We don't wanna wake him up...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Should we pretend to purify the King?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: You've made it at last. You did even better than I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, now comes the final and most important step of the ceremony. Please use the power of the sacred flame to cleanse the Mountain King of Abyssal filth!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: There's no need this time.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Such strong Abyssal power! What is that thing?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Kinich! What is the meaning of this!?

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Is that... a Beastly Rift!?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Chief Wayna, Elder Trinidad, this is about to get a little dangerous. You should step back.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: What do you think you're doing?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Solving the Mountain King issue.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: You mean... By having him torn to pieces by Rifthounds!?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: No, stop! We can't let that happen!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Foolish locust! Can't you see? We're trying to shove your Locust King into the Beastly Rift!

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: But... But...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Chief Wayna, and Elder Trinidad. This is the only way.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Can you promise me that no harm will come to the Mountain King?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I can't guarantee it, but I'm fairly confident.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, this is not what we agreed on! You must cleanse the Mountain King of every last trace of Abyssal contamination!

choices.text: I've changed my mind. I don't want the King to die.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Okay, I see what this is! You've been in cahoots this whole time!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: You imbecile! What have you done!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no... The device is destroyed!

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: You forced my hand. I had no choice...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Elder Trinidad... Wh—What are you doing!?

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: No! The Mountain King is waking up... He will cause even more casualties...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Everyone, out! Now!

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Hahahaha... It seems there is only one way to awaken you all from your willful blindness... More sacrifices must be made.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Take me, O Mountain King! Take me as your next sacrifice!

choices.text: This was Kinich's idea. It has nothing to do with me.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Hey, bet you're surprised to see me? Didn't think I'd be coming, did ya?

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: I was all packed up and ready to go, but then I thought, I wonder if the ceremony will go any differently with a new flame bearer? So yeah, here I am again!

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: I still owe you for that picture you took. So once you start, I'll be dancing to cheer you on.

dialogues.speaker: Thiago
dialogues.text: Don't be nervous. You'll do great.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you've come at just the right time. I have some good news for you...

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Trinidad's condition has stabilized. He suffered burns on much of his body, but we believe he'll survive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess that's the best news we could hope for...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon has to ask, is everyone in your tribe such a risk-taker? First Kinich, then Elder Trinidad... Is this the Scions of the Canopy's adventurous spirit in action?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: We're simply not afraid to charge ahead into the unknown.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is Kinich okay?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: He's fine, don't worry. He's gone to check on the Mountain King — something most mysterious has happened.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: After the incident yesterday, a transparent shell has formed around the Mountain King's body. We don't understand the mechanism behind it, but this shell appears to insulate him against the influence of Abyssal power.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: It is somewhat akin to a scab, in that it stops the Abyssal energy within him from bleeding out, while also preventing further Abyssal energy from seeping in and infecting him.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: We've never seen anything like it. The tribe's most senior elders believe it was caused when he was burned by the sacred flame, similar to the way burned wood becomes charcoal.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: I think their theory makes sense. After all, we've never thrown the Mountain King directly into the sacred flame before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, so it's made a barrier against Abyssal energy? That's... a good thing, right?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: It's practically a miracle, from what we've seen of it so far. It means that the Mountain King's level of Abyssal energy is now stable. No longer will we need to perform an annual cleansing ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! That's amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Was it really just the power of the sacred flame?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: I know what you're thinking. The young people in the tribe are already speculating that yesterday's ceremony was a Turnfire Night like none other in our history.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Because you and Kinich... You summoned the very flame that appears in our ancient legends. A great, transparent ball of fire.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: And that fire is what saved the Mountain King.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! So that was the real Turnfire?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Haha, I may be the chief of this tribe, but I've only ever known the Turnfire as a concept in our legends. I cannot answer that question.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: If anyone can answer it, I suspect it would be the bearer of the Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo name. He is in the Mountain King's cave as we speak.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... So, Kinich then. Why don't we go see how he's doing?

talks.objective: Find Kinich and talk to him

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Kinich!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Hey yourselves. You two doing okay after yesterday?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We were gonna ask you the same question... You scared Paimon half to death when you rushed into the fire.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Sorry, I couldn't just stand and watch the Mountain King get burned alive.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: So you thought you'd try and extinguish the sacred flame with Dendro? Or was that an attempt to make the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw die of laughter?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The sacred flame only possesses a fraction of the Pyro Archon's power. It's not as if I was fighting the Pyro Archon herself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kinich... When you went into the flames, were you intending to... uh...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Intending to what?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: To, um... do the same thing as Burkina...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Sacrifice myself? Of course not. My focus was on keeping the Mountain King alive, not on what it would cost.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: But now I'm curious. What made you think I was going to sacrifice myself?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... Because everyone's saying the Turnfire is what saved the King last night...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And Ponche's theory was that summoning the Turnfire is a tit-for-tat exchange, right? So Paimon thought you'd decided to pay for it with your life...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: So you've heard that rumor too.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I can't say for sure. What happened yesterday was a first for me too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if even you don't know, there's probably no one in the world who does.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: What I would say is, if that really was the power of the Turnfire, I'd sooner believe that the Mountain King summoned it himself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Mountain King? Then... what price did he pay?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The core meaning of "price" is not atonement or compensation, but what you're willing to give up in order to obtain what you want.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: It's easy to die for your sins, much harder to live with the guilt and keep on going. In the end, the Mountain King chose the latter option — for Burkina, and for the tribe. That's the price he paid.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright... So how is the Mountain King doing now?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Health-wise, there's nothing to worry about. He'll enter a fighting stance whenever we set foot in his territory.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: But his attacks are gentler now, and not as crazed as before. Like he said yesterday, he just intends to be a sparring partner for people to practice with.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You said "health-wise." Is something else bothering you?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Yeah. I tried communicating with him again, but he didn't respond.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Hmph, we daresay that Locust King has well and truly lost its mind. The lights are on, but nobody is home.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Its body remains fighting fit thanks to the perverse power of the Abyss, but time has been less kind to its soul... It was ground to a pulp long ago!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we saw him come back to his senses yesterday...

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: That was merely one last burst of brain activity before it croaked. As you humans would say, it went out with a bang.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, come on! Stop being such a doomer. Paimon bets the Mountain King has finally let go of the tragedies of the past now, and is focusing on moving forward!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's why he doesn't have time to chat with us. He's too busy thinking about the future!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: #Heh, well, at least it means my fellow tribespeople can move forward now, too. Thank you for your help, {NICKNAME}. I owe you one.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nah, you already gave me that "gift."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's right. You caught Enjou for us, remember?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: But he ended up being completely useless. It's not a fair trade if you lost out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh, that's on him. It's not your fault he's useless! Besides, we're friends now. You don't owe us anything.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Friends? But your friendship is an even more valuable gift. I can't in good conscience accept it for free...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: So promise me, if you need anything in the future, you'll come to me.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: For you, I'll do anything.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: ACHOO! Ahem... So in the end, only poor little Huni got the sad ending?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Yeah! Everyone's happy, except me. First Nanna, then my Dad... Why does everyone in my family have to suffer?

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Huni... It'll be okay. Your dad will get better soon.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Toba, you're my friend, so I shouldn't say this to your face. But it was all the Mountain King's fault.

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Ehh!?

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Now hold your horses, kiddo. If you promise not to fight, Uncle Sanka will tell you a story.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: ...Okay, before you roll your eyes out of your skull, I promise you can trust me. I almost got my eyebrows burned off by the Turnfire after last time. That's why I came back, to make it up to you!

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: ...Alright, I'll just get to the point. Do you know what Uncle Sanka loves the most about your people?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Your extreme sports.

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: On my first day here, I got hit by someone falling out of the sky. I believe you call it "bungee jumping"?

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: It's a dangerous sport, to be sure, but the courage it took to make the jump impressed the heck out of me. So I introduced myself to the jumper, we made friends, and I even helped treat her wounds.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Aw. Such a nice friend.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Of course. Anyway, the good times didn't last, 'cause I got captured by a powerful foe, so we had to part ways for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: In the hands of the enemy, I was scorned, scolded, and nearly given away as a gift. Oh, it was so humiliating! A horrible experience to look back on.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: "Why does Uncle Sanka always have to suffer?" I thought. So I feel your pain, Huni. I was in the same position.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: But in the end, I made it through, and I left all of those painful memories in the past. I even managed to reunite with my friend!

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: Uh... Is that it?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: The moral of the story is to look forward in life, right? Yeah, we've heard that one millions of times. Sorry, Uncle Sanka, but you're not cut out to be a teacher.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Very smart, Huni. But not quite smart enough.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: What I'm trying to tell you is that after I reunited with my friend, I found her injuries were all healed, but she really missed her family. So, I thought you might like to see her too.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: She's right behind you. Turn around and see.

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Another trick about not turning back? I'm not falling for that one again!

talks.objective: Head back to the Mountain King's cave

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I still need time to prepare.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Very well. Then come back when you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Mighty outlanders, the time has finally come. You know what must be done.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Please remember, you must cleanse as much Abyssal energy as you can. This is the only way to prolong the Mountain King's slumber.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: I am sure you have what it takes.

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME}! You're finally here! I even dragged my uncle out to watch the ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: Although I'd hoped for the Malipo name-bearer to perform this ceremony, that was never anything to do with you. So please don't take it personally.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: I got thinking last night, and I realized: If the lesson of Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo is to look forwards, then I should accept that my book is gone, and start anew.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: Besides, I'll have even more to write about this time, given this will be our first Turnfire ceremony featuring a flame bearer from another land.

dialogues.speaker: Ponche
dialogues.text: I'll be taking detailed notes.

dialogues.speaker: Toba
dialogues.text: #Good luck, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME}! You got this!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The following day, in the Scions of the Canopy tribe...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I saw you leave the ceremony site, and was worried you might get lost, so I came to check up on you.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Are you in trouble? Let me help you out, then escort you back.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I just need a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Sure. I'll wait here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's head back.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Kay. Let's go.
